props.gloss_en: R' Eliezer: weapons are ornaments for him
the Sages' premise: weapons cease in the days of the Messiah
R' Eliezer (version 1): [they cease] because they will not be needed
as it is said: 'nation shall not lift up sword against nation' (Isa 2:4)
Abaye: it is like a lamp at noon
Shmuel: there is no difference between this world and the days of the Messiah except subjugation of the exiles alone
as it is said: 'for the poor shall not cease from the midst of the land' (Deut 15:11)
R' Chiyya bar Abba: all the prophets prophesied only for the days of the Messiah
but for the world to come -- 'no eye has seen, God, aside from You' (Isa 64:3)
R' Eliezer (version 2): even in the days of the Messiah weapons do not cease
the reason of R' Eliezer, who said they are ornaments: as it is written 'gird your sword upon your thigh, mighty one, your glory and your splendour' (Ps 45:4)
a verse does not depart from its plain meaning

a person should learn and afterwards reason

objections.gloss_en: וכי מאחר דתכשיטין הן לו, מפני מה הן בטלין לימות המשיח? -- if they are ornaments, why will they cease in the days of the Messiah? (as the baraita reports it)

objections.gloss_en: ותהוי לנוי בעלמא! -- though not needed for war, let them remain merely as ornament

answered_by.gloss_en: מידי דהוה אשרגא בטיהרא -- like a lamp at noon (= p_shraga_betihara)

objections.gloss_en: ואיכא דאמרי: אמרו לו לרבי אליעזר: וכי מאחר דתכשיטין הן לו, מפני מה הן בטלין לימות המשיח?

answered_by.gloss_en: אף לימות המשיח אינן בטלין -- even in the days of the Messiah they do not cease (= p_einan_betelin)
